content:
The test image shows soybean pods that are brown, dried/shrunken, and poorly filled, with dead stems and no leaves. This suggests premature plant death or pod blight. Top candidates: Charcoal_Rot, Sudden_death_syndrome, Diaporthe, Brown_Stem_Rot, Phomopsis.

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.
The Phomopsis reference (top-right panel) shows dried brown pods hanging on stems — very similar to the test image. Let me check a few more candidates.
Now let me look at a couple more candidates to confirm.

**Analysis summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Affected part: Pods and stems
- Color: Uniform brown/tan, dried
- Pattern: Shrunken, poorly filled pods still attached to dead brown stems
- No leaves (defoliated), no white cottony growth, no obvious dark pycnidia spots
- Fuzzy hairy texture (normal soybean pod surface)

**Candidate evaluation:**
- **Phomopsis**: Top-right panel of reference shows nearly identical dried brown pods hanging on stems. Phomopsis pod blight causes exactly this — shrunken brown pods, premature plant death at pod fill stage. Best visual match.
- **Anthracnose**: Also shows brown dried pods but with more visible dark acervuli/spots — not seen here.
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Shows bleached/gray stems — test image shows brown stems, not the characteristic gray bleaching.
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Primary symptom is interveinal leaf chlorosis/necrosis, not pod browning.
- **Brown_Stem_Rot, Fusarium, Phytophthora**: Root/stem rot diseases, don't match pod-focused symptom.
- All leaf-based diseases (Cercospora, Frogeye, Soybean_rust, etc.) are clearly ruled out.

The test image most closely matches **Phomopsis** pod blight — uniformly brown, shrunken pods on dead stems with no dark spots, matching the Phomopsis reference (top-right panel) very closely.

The Phomopsis reference (top-right panel) shows nearly identical dried brown pods hanging on stems. No white mold, no dark acervuli (ruling out Anthracnose), no gray bleaching of stems (ruling out Charcoal Rot)."}
